LICENCE NOT CONFIRMED: elevate.exe

elevate.exe sits in the resources folder of the Windows build. electron-builder places it there from its NSIS bundle, for the installer.
It is not a dependency in package.json, and the package-lock scan does not see it.
It was checked again in October 2026, now that electron-builder's NSIS cache (nsis-3.0.4.1) is on this computer:
- The program's own version information names the company Johannes Passing, the product Elevate Application, the copyright (C) 2007 and the original file name Elevate.exe.
- The author's page (jpassing.com, "Launch elevated processes from the command line") says the source code may be used under the terms of the MIT License, and links https://github.com/jpassing/elevate, whose licence GitHub lists as MIT.
- That repository's LICENSE.md is the MIT text with the year and the copyright holder left blank. The copyright line below therefore comes from the program's own version information.
- Not checked: that the elevate.exe in the NSIS bundle is an unchanged build of that source.

Before a release: the developer confirms this, replaces this file with the licence text below (without this note), and then sets this entry's status to confirmed in scripts/third-party-notices.mjs.
While this entry is unconfirmed, scripts/third-party-notices.mjs prints a warning and marks the entry in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. With PLENUM_RELEASE=1 the build fails until it is confirmed.
